citation: Comer, B. M.; Li, J.; Abild-Pedersen, F.; Bajdich, M.; Winther, K. T. Unraveling Electronic Trends in O* and OH* Surface Adsorption in the MO2 Transition-Metal Oxide Series. J. Phys. Chem. C 2022, 126, 7903-7909.
system: 33 MO2 rutile transition-metal oxides (3d, 4d, 5d), +4 oxidation state, (110) CUS-site and (100) top-site adsorption, 1x1 high-coverage cells
method: VASP, PBE+U (3d metals only, see hubbard_u.json; 4d/5d at plain PBE), 500 eV cutoff, 8x4x1 k-points, fmax=0.02 eV/A (0.07 eV/A for O*/CdO2(100))
reference_state: DeltaE/G referenced to gas-phase H2O and H2: H2O(g) - H2(g) + * -> O*,  H2O(g) - 0.5 H2(g) + * -> OH*

files.adsorption_energies.csv: Table S3 -- all 132 rows (33 metals x 2 facets x {O,OH}), raw DeltaE_ads and ZPE/TS-corrected DeltaG_ads, eV
files.hubbard_u.json: Table S1 -- U values applied to the 3d metals
files.free_energy_corrections.json: Table S2 -- ZPE/Hvib/TS corrections used to go from DeltaE to DeltaG
files.jp2c02381.pdf: main text -- NOT YET SAVED, drop the file in this folder
files.jp2c02381_si_001.pdf: Supporting Information -- NOT YET SAVED, drop the file in this folder

caveats: Magnetic structure is constrained: empty*, OH*, and O* surfaces are forced to share the same magnetic configuration (SI Fig. S1) -- an MLIP comparison has no spin state at all, so this is a real methodological gap, not just a numerical one, for the early-3d high-spin metals (V, Cr, Mn, Fe).
CdO2(100)/O* was relaxed to a looser 0.07 eV/A instead of the paper's usual 0.02 eV/A -- flagged in case a tight-fmax MLIP comparison lands suspiciously off for that one row.

This repo's rutile TiO2(110) benchmark already uses seed_standoff=0.5 (see scripts/o_adsorption_benchmark.py); this paper's TiO2(110) O* value (4.55 eV) is a second, independent literature point for that same oxide/facet, distinct from the Zhao & Kulik 2019 value (4.43 eV) already wired into OXIDES in that script.
